title: One Barrel of Oil, Explained in Numbers
description: Brent annual averages are rounded EIA figures. A barrel is 42 US gallons.

beats.text: One barrel of oil. Forty-two US gallons, about one hundred and fifty-nine litres.
And its price can swing wildly. In April twenty twenty, the US benchmark, W T I, closed below zero, at minus thirty-seven dollars. Two years later, Brent touched about one hundred and thirty-nine.
Zoom out and the pattern is clear. Brent's yearly average rose from forty-two dollars in twenty twenty to over one hundred in twenty twenty-two.
That is a rise of one hundred and forty percent. After that peak, the average slipped back by about eighteen dollars.
Who makes all this oil? Three countries lead the world: the United States, Saudi Arabia, and Russia. Much of it flows east, to China, the biggest crude importer.
And a barrel does not stay crude. Refiners split it into fuel. About nineteen gallons of gasoline, twelve of diesel, and four of jet fuel.
So the price at the pump follows crude, with a delay. Watch the barrel, and you can see the pump coming.
